sections.h2: What the Hunterdon County Clerk does when a house sells
sections.html:
Every Hunterdon County deed and mortgage passes through the County Clerk, an elected office that calls itself the Keeper of the Records. Staff in the recording division examine each document for form, dates, signatures, acknowledgment and the property's location. Fees and transfer taxes are settled at the counter when the paper is filed. After that the clerk stamps a recording date, enters the document in the permanent index, sends an abstract of the deed to the local assessor, and hands the original back to the owner.

The office is at 71 Main Street in Flemington, and the mailing address is PO Box 2900, Flemington, NJ 08822. Counter service runs on weekdays until half past four, and the main line is (908) 788-1221. The clerk accepts e-filing, which lets whoever handles your closing submit the deed electronically, and posts a deed fraud warning worth reading before you sign anything.

State law sets the transfer fee, and the clerk takes it at the counter in addition to ordinary recording charges. Each slice of the price carries its own rate, quoted for every $500 or part of $500. The rates below apply when the total price is over $350,000.

Realty transfer fee per $500 of consideration, sales above $350,000
Slice of the sale priceCharge per $500
First $150,000$2.90
$150,000 to $200,000$4.25
$200,000 to $550,000$4.80
$550,000 to $850,000$5.30
$850,000 to $1,000,000$5.80
Every dollar over $1,000,000$6.05

A sale at $350,000 or less uses lower rates. A residential sale priced over $1,000,000 adds a separate seller charge, the graduated percent fee, equal to 1 percent of the whole price and rising in steps to 3.5 percent past $3,500,000. Call the clerk to confirm which fee schedule applies to a deed over $1,000,000. For an exact number, run the price through the transfer fee calculator the clerk links.

sections.h2: Deeds exempt from the transfer fee
sections.html:
The state form carries a longer exemption list. These entries matter most to families and estates:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • An executor or administrator conveying to a devisee or heir to distribute the estate under a will or intestate succession.
  • Husband and wife, civil union partners, or parent and child.
  • A deed recorded inside 90 days of a divorce decree dissolving the marriage.
  • Paper that only gives or releases security for a debt, or fixes an earlier recorded deed.
  • A conveyance made on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

An exemption has to be explained in detail on the affidavit. A simple exemption symbol is not enough.

The clerk will not record a deed unless it recites the consideration or carries an affidavit that states it. Consideration includes the money paid, the value of anything else given, and the balance of any mortgage the buyer assumes. Falsifying it is a fourth-degree crime under the state form's warning.

Because the clerk forwards each deed to the municipal assessor, recording feeds directly into the tax roll. Hunterdon has 26 municipalities, and the state's 2025 table shows effective tax rates running from 1.782 in East Amwell to 3.483 in Hampton. Flemington, the county seat, is at a general rate of 2.736 and an effective rate of 2.984. Lambertville is at 1.902 effective, Clinton Town at 2.808 and High Bridge at 3.152.

The effective rate puts every town on the same footing, so a low general rate does not by itself mean a low bill. Bethlehem Township shows a general rate of 2.021 and an effective rate of 2.350, while Milford shows 4.027 general and 2.944 effective. Look up your own municipality before you choose a list price.

The 2025 estimate is 131,781 residents and 50,860 households. Owners occupy 85.1 percent of the homes, those homes are valued at a median $517,200, and a typical household earns $141,715. Gross rent in the middle of the range is $1,687. With so many owners, most sales are a family selling the home they live in, often a house with a well, a septic system or a long driveway that buyers will ask about.

Hunterdon has about 1,412 miles of public roads, and most of them, roughly 1,059 miles, are kept up by the municipalities. The county maintains about 238 miles and the state about 115, so the road at your driveway may belong to the town, the county or the state. Know which before you answer a buyer's question about plowing and repairs.

The clerk's records go back to 1785, and the Record Room is open to the public on weekdays. Help from the Search Room staff is available by appointment at (908) 788-1380. Older records are being redacted to protect identities, with an online system planned after that work ends.

Sellers use these records to confirm the vesting deed, find an open mortgage that needs a release, or locate a recorded lien before a closing. The clerk's recording page also links a homeowner's guide to good deeds, a document reference manual and mortgage foreclosure help for owners behind on payments.

Hunterdon County does not take part in the Homeless Trust Fund, so budget no charge for it when you add up recording costs.

sections.h2: What to confirm with the clerk before closing
sections.html:
• The current recording fee schedule, since only the transfer fee rates are reproduced here.
  • Whether the deed needs the seller's Affidavit of Consideration, required above $1,000,000 or when an exemption is claimed.
  • Who signs the affidavit: the form allows a grantor, a legal representative, or a title or lending officer.
  • How to deliver the package: at the counter, by mail or electronically.
  • The block and lot number, which the form requires and the municipal assessor can supply.
  • Whether the title company or attorney already holds the vesting deed, so the new deed's description matches it.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the deed, the affidavit and the transfer fee still go through the clerk in the same way, so the same checklist applies.

In practice the order runs like this: the closing attorney or title company prepares the deed, you sign it with any affidavit, the package goes to the counter or in electronically with the fees, and the clerk stamps the recording date. Once recorded, the clerk sends the deed abstract to the assessor and returns the original to the new owner. Ask your closing contact who is delivering the package and on what day, so nothing sits waiting while the fee clock and your payoff both keep running.

faqs.q: Where does a Hunterdon County deed get recorded?
faqs.a: In the County Clerk's recording section on Main Street in Flemington. Call (908) 788-1221 before you go, since the office keeps weekday hours only.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Hunterdon County sale?
faqs.a: Sellers do. The recorder's block on the state form is labeled as paid by the seller, and the fee arrives at the counter with the deed.

faqs.q: Is a deed from an estate to an heir exempt from the transfer fee?
faqs.a: Yes, when the executor or administrator is carrying out a will or the intestacy laws. That case is listed among the form's exemptions.

faqs.q: Which Hunterdon County town has the highest effective tax rate?
faqs.a: Hampton leads the state's 2025 table at 3.483, while East Amwell sits at the bottom with 1.782.

faqs.q: Can I look up old Hunterdon County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Recorded instruments run from 1785 forward, and the public can visit the Record Room and the Search Room on weekdays.
